examples.ko: 옆방에서 사람들이 두런두런 이야기하는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear people talking in low voices in the next room.

examples.ko: 부엌에서 엄마와 이모가 두런두런 얘기를 나눠요.
examples.en: Mom and my aunt are chatting quietly in the kitchen.
Since dawn there was a low murmur of voices in the yard.
We talked softly about old times all night.
The murmur of voices woke me up.

examples.ko: 할머니들이 마루에 앉아 두런두런 이야기를 나누고 계세요.
examples.en: The grandmothers are sitting on the porch chatting in low voices.

explain: 여럿이 낮은 목소리로 조용히 이야기하는 소리나 모습이에요. '소곤소곤'은 비밀 이야기처럼 아주 작게 말하는 느낌이고, '두런두런'은 정답고 편안하게 이야기하는 분위기예요.

phrases.en: I chatted quietly with my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조용하고 정답게 대화하는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a quiet, friendly conversation.

phrases.en: I could hear low voices until late at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가까운 곳에서 낮게 들리는 말소리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for low voices heard from somewhere nearby.

phrases.en: In the evening I had a quiet talk with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이야기하다'보다 조금 더 차분하고 글 같은 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sounds a bit calmer and more written than 이야기하다.

explain_en: It describes several people talking quietly in low voices. '소곤소곤' feels like whispering a secret, while '두런두런' has a warm, relaxed atmosphere.

examples.en: The villain boss in the movie escaped.
The police finally caught the leader of the thieves.

examples.ko: 아이들은 놀이터에서 서로 두목 노릇을 하고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: Kids at the playground each want to play the boss.

examples.ko: 그 조직의 두목은 아직 밝혀지지 않았어요.
examples.en: The head of that organization has not been identified yet.

examples.ko: 부하가 해적 두목에게 보물 상자를 건넸어요.
examples.en: The henchman handed the treasure chest to the pirate captain.

examples.ko: 우리 형은 어릴 때 동네 꼬마들의 두목이었어요.
examples.en: When he was young, my older brother was the boss of the neighborhood kids.

explain: 나쁜 무리의 우두머리라는 느낌이 강해요. 영화나 만화에 많이 나오고, 회사 사장님에게 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있어요. 좋은 단체의 대표는 '대표', '회장', '리더'라고 해요. 아이들 놀이에서 쓰는 '대장'은 귀여운 말이에요.

phrases.en: The police caught the boss of the crime ring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 조직과 함께 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, used with bad organizations.

phrases.en: In the movie, the pirate chief looks for treasure.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화나 만화 속 우두머리를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for leaders in movies and cartoons.

phrases.en: The boss shouted at his men.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부하'와 같이 나오는 이야기에서 자주 쓰는 문장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common sentence in stories that also have 부하 (subordinates).

explain_en: It strongly feels like the head of a bad group. It appears often in movies and comics, and calling a company president this would be rude. The head of a good organization is called '대표', '회장', or '리더'. In kids' play, '대장' is the cute word.

examples.ko: 옛날 이야기에는 힘센 마당쇠가 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Strong male servants named Madangsoe often appear in old tales.

examples.ko: 우리 집에서는 아빠가 마당쇠 역할을 해요.
examples.en: At our home, Dad plays the role of the one who does all the heavy work.

examples.ko: 회사에서 늘 궂은일을 하는 마당쇠가 되기 싫어요.
examples.en: I don't want to become the office workhorse who always does the dirty work.

examples.ko: 이사하는 날 남동생이 마당쇠처럼 짐을 날랐어요.
examples.en: On moving day, my younger brother carried the luggage like a workhorse.

examples.ko: 마당쇠 같은 친구라 부탁하면 다 들어줘요.
examples.en: He's such a helpful workhorse of a friend that he grants every request.
He is known as our village's go-to man for hard work.

explain: 원래는 집안의 허드렛일을 맡던 남자 하인을 말해요. 요즘은 힘들고 궂은일을 도맡아 하는 사람을 비유해서 쓰는데, 낮춰 보는 느낌이 있어서 남에게 쓰면 실례가 될 수 있어요. 자기 자신을 농담처럼 말할 때 쓰는 경우가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 이사하는 날 제가 마당쇠 노릇을 했어요.
phrases.en: I played the workhorse on moving day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '노릇'이 붙어 힘든 일을 도맡아 하는 역할을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '노릇' means playing the role of the one who does all the hard work.

phrases.en: He is like a workhorse at the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 궂은일을 다 맡는 사람을 비유하는데 낮춰 보는 느낌이 있어서 남에게는 조심해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes someone who takes on all the dirty work, but it can sound belittling, so be careful using it about others.

phrases.en: I do housework like a workhorse every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 자신을 농담처럼 말할 때 자연스러운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is natural when joking about yourself.

explain_en: It originally meant a male servant who did the household chores. Today it figuratively refers to someone who takes on all the hard, dirty jobs, but it can sound belittling and be rude when used about others. It is more natural when you joke about yourself.

examples.en: My grandmother lived alone all her life with no children.
My friend has no children, so she adores her nephew.
That couple has no children but lives happily.
They say that in the old days, families without children worried a lot.
I went to a group that helps elderly people with no children.

examples.ko: 무자식이 되고 싶어서 된 건 아니에요.
examples.en: It's not that I wanted to have no children.

explain: 자식이 없다는 사실을 조금 딱딱하게 말하는 단어예요. 사람 앞에서 말할 때는 '자녀가 없다'가 더 부드럽게 들려요. '무자식 상팔자'라는 속담으로 가장 많이 만나요.

phrases.example: 아이 키우느라 힘들 때마다 부모님은 무자식 상팔자라고 말씀하세요.
phrases.en: No children is the best fortune.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자식 걱정이 끊이지 않으니 차라리 자식이 없는 게 편하다는 속담이에요. 진심이라기보다 힘들 때 푸념하듯 말하는 경우가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning that children bring endless worry, so having none is easier. It is usually a half-joking complaint rather than a sincere belief.

explain_en: It states the fact of having no children in a rather blunt way. When speaking about a person, '자녀가 없다' sounds softer. You most often meet it in the proverb '무자식 상팔자'.

examples.ko: 버르장머리 없이 어른께 말하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not talk to elders so rudely.
That child has no manners at all.

examples.ko: 자꾸 그러면 그 버르장머리를 고쳐 줄 거예요.
examples.en: If you keep doing that, I'll straighten out that bad attitude of yours.
Who taught you such bad manners?

examples.ko: 어릴 때 버르장머리를 잘 잡아 줘야 해요.
examples.en: You have to set good manners right when they are young.

examples.ko: 저 버르장머리 좀 보세요, 인사도 안 하네요.
examples.en: Look at that attitude, he doesn't even say hello.

explain: '버릇'보다 거칠고 속된 말이라서 예의 없는 태도를 나무랄 때 많이 써요. '버르장머리가 없다', '버르장머리를 고치다'처럼 말해요. 어른이 아랫사람에게 하는 말이라 윗사람에게 쓰면 무례해요.

phrases.en: I want to correct my younger sibling's bad manners.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 태도를 바로잡는다는 뜻으로, 보통 윗사람이 아랫사람에게 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to correct bad behavior; usually said by someone older about someone younger.

phrases.example: 어른께 버르장머리 없는 행동을 하면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You must not behave rudely toward elders.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예의 없는 행동을 거칠게 나무랄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A blunt way to criticize rude behavior.

phrases.en: That child has no manners.
phrases.nuance_ko: '버르장머리'보다 덜 거칠고 더 널리 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less harsh and more widely used than 버르장머리.

explain_en: It is a rougher, more colloquial word than '버릇', mostly used to scold rude behavior. You say '버르장머리가 없다' or '버르장머리를 고치다'. It is spoken by elders to younger people, so using it toward a superior is rude.

t90.ax: Who taught you such bad manners?

examples.ko: 진시황은 불로장생을 꿈꾸며 약을 찾았다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the First Emperor of Qin searched for medicine, dreaming of eternal youth.

examples.ko: 요즘 사람들은 불로장생보다 건강하게 오래 사는 걸 원해요.
examples.en: These days people want to live long and healthy more than eternal youth.
I asked my grandmother what the secret to eternal youth is.

examples.ko: 이 약초가 불로장생에 좋다는 말은 믿기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to believe the claim that this herb is good for eternal youth.

examples.ko: 불로장생은 오래전부터 사람들이 꿈꿔 온 이야기예요.
examples.en: Eternal youth is a dream people have had for a very long time.
Everyone hopes for eternal youth, but it's impossible.

explain: '장수'는 오래 사는 것이고 '불로장생'은 늙지 않고 오래 산다는 꿈같은 이야기에 써요. 옛이야기나 진시황, 약초 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Kings of old dreamed of eternal youth.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불로장생'을 목적어로 써서 늙지 않고 오래 살기를 바란다는 뜻을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the word as an object to say someone wishes to never age and to live long.

phrases.example: 불로장생의 꿈은 지금도 많은 사람들의 이야기에 나와요.
phrases.en: The dream of eternal youth still appears in many people's stories.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의'로 이어서 '꿈'을 꾸미는 말이에요. 이야기나 글에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Linked with '의' to describe a dream; common in stories and writing.

phrases.example: 이 약이 불로장생의 비결이라고 광고하지만 믿기 어려워요.
phrases.en: The ad says this medicine is the secret to eternal youth, but it's hard to believe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 늙지 않고 오래 사는 방법을 말할 때 쓰고, 조금 과장하거나 농담처럼 쓰기도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a way of never aging; often used with exaggeration or as a joke.

explain_en: '장수' simply means living long, whereas '불로장생' is for the dream of not aging and living forever. It often appears in old tales and in stories about the First Emperor or magic herbs.

en: to treasure; to cherish; to coddle

examples.en: My grandmother dotes on her youngest grandson.
That bag is something my father treasured.
My parents dote on me so much that it feels like a burden.
I carefully wiped my new camera as if it were a treasure.
I gave my younger sibling the doll I had cherished so much.

examples.ko: 제가 애지중지해서 키운 화분이 꽃을 피웠어요.
examples.en: The potted plant I raised with so much care has bloomed.

explain: '아끼다'보다 더 아주 소중히 다루는 느낌이고, 사람과 물건에 모두 써요. '애지중지 키우다'처럼 '애지중지'만 부사처럼 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: My parents raised the youngest with great care.
phrases.nuance_ko: '애지중지'만 부사처럼 써서 아주 소중히 대하는 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used alone like an adverb to add a feeling of deep care.

phrases.en: It's a letter I've kept with great care.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 소중하게 보관한 물건에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something kept dear for a long time.

phrases.en: I treasure my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉽고 일상적인 말이에요. 느낌은 '애지중지'보다 덜 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and more everyday, but less intense than 'aejijungji'.

explain_en: It feels stronger than '아끼다', meaning to handle something with great care, and it works for both people and objects. '애지중지' alone is also used like an adverb, as in '애지중지 키우다'.

examples.en: Parents raise their children with love.

examples.ko: 혼자 아이를 양육하는 일은 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: Raising a child alone is not easy.
My grandmother raised me from when I was little.
You need patience when you raise a child.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 아이를 함께 양육하고 있어요.
examples.en: The two of them are raising the child together.

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 아이를 양육하는 직원에게 휴가를 줘요.
examples.en: Our company gives leave to employees who are raising children.

explain: '양육하다'는 뉴스, 서류, 정책 이야기에서 자주 나오는 딱딱한 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '아이를 키우다'라고 해요. 보통 사람이 아이에게 쓰고, 동물이나 식물에는 '키우다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I raise my child alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '양육하다'와 같은 뜻으로, 일상 대화에서 훨씬 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 양육하다 but used much more in daily conversation.

phrases.en: Child-rearing costs add up when you raise a child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이를 키우는 데 드는 돈을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The money needed to bring up a child.

phrases.example: 이 아이의 양육을 할머니가 맡고 있어요.
phrases.en: The grandmother is in charge of raising this child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 아이를 책임지고 키우는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say who takes responsibility for raising a child.

explain_en: 양육하다 is a formal word you see in news, documents and policy talk. In everyday conversation Koreans say '아이를 키우다'. It is used for children, while animals and plants take '키우다'.

examples.en: My grandmother is a well-known strong woman at the market.

examples.ko: 그분은 회사를 혼자 일으킨 여장부라고 불려요.
examples.en: She is called a heroine for building a company on her own.
True to her bold character, she handled even hard tasks bravely.

examples.ko: 어머니는 몸집은 작아도 마음은 여장부 같아요.
examples.en: My mother is small, but she has the heart of a heroine.

examples.ko: 남자 직원들도 그 여장부 앞에서는 말을 아꼈어요.
examples.en: Even the male staff watched their words in front of that formidable woman.

examples.ko: 그녀는 마을 일을 도맡아 하던 여장부였어요.
examples.en: She was a strong woman who took charge of the village's affairs.

explain: 배포가 크고 씩씩한 여자를 칭찬할 때 써요. 짝이 되는 말은 '대장부'예요. 다른 사람을 높이는 말이라 본인에게는 잘 안 써요.

phrases.example: 그분은 일할 때 정말 여장부 같아요.
phrases.en: She really seems like a heroine when she works.
phrases.nuance_ko: 씩씩하고 배포 큰 여자를 보고 느낌을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a bold, spirited woman.

phrases.en: Smiling even in hardship is just like a true heroine.
phrases.nuance_ko: '여장부'에 어울리는 모습일 때 칭찬으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment when someone acts worthy of the title.
phrases.en_equiv: to be worthy of a heroine

phrases.en: My mother is known in the neighborhood as a heroine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람들 사이에서 그렇게 알려졌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means she's widely known as such among others.
phrases.en_equiv: to be known as a heroine

explain_en: It praises a woman who is bold and spirited. Its counterpart is '대장부'. Since it is praise for others, people rarely use it about themselves.

t90.ax: My mother is small, but she has the heart of a heroine.

examples.en: My stepmother and I are like friends.
My stepmother packs me a lunch box every day.
She calls her stepmother 'Mom'.
My stepmother took care of my birthday.
My stepmother treats me like her own daughter.
I learned cooking from my stepmother when I was young.

explain: 아버지가 재혼해서 생긴 어머니를 말해요. 직접 부를 때는 '어머니', '엄마'라고 해요. '새어머니'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: My stepmother treats me like her own daughter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의붓어머니'보다 부드럽고 일상에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer than 의붓어머니 and more common in daily speech.

phrases.en: My stepmother made delicious food for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높임 조사 '께서'를 붙여 존댓말로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds the honorific particle 께서 to show respect.

phrases.en: I get along well with my stepmother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가족 관계를 이야기할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when talking about family relationships.
phrases.en_equiv: to get along with one's stepmother

explain_en: It refers to the mother you gain when your father remarries. When addressing her directly, people say '어머니' or '엄마'. It is also called '새어머니'.

en: way of speaking; being in the habit of saying things a certain way

examples.en: My grandmother says 'Health comes first' like a catchphrase.
Saying he's tired is a habit of that friend.

examples.ko: 입버릇으로 하는 말이니까 신경 쓰지 마세요.
examples.en: It's just something he always says, so don't mind it.
It's good to fix a bad speaking habit.
'Let's go together later' was my dad's usual line.
When I changed what I habitually say, my mood got better too.

explain: '입버릇처럼 말하다'로 가장 많이 써요. 같은 말을 습관적으로 자꾸 하는 것을 말하고, '말버릇'과 비슷하게 쓰여요. 진심이라기보다 습관처럼 나오는 말이라는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: He keeps saying "I'm busy" out of habit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 말을 습관처럼 자주 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means repeatedly saying the same thing out of habit.

phrases.en: Saying sorry has become a habit of mine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 말이 습관으로 굳었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a certain phrase has become a fixed habit.

phrases.en: I have a verbal habit of saying "really."
phrases.nuance_ko: 입버릇과 비슷하지만 말투 전반의 습관을 넓게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 입버릇 but covers speech habits more broadly.

explain_en: The most common use is '입버릇처럼 말하다'. It describes saying the same thing again and again out of habit, and it is used much like '말버릇'. It carries a sense that the words come out by habit rather than from real feeling.

examples.en: When the conductor raised his hand, the performance began.

examples.ko: 우리 학교 합창단의 지휘자는 음악 선생님이에요.
examples.en: The conductor of our school choir is the music teacher.

examples.ko: 그 지휘자는 세계 여러 나라에서 공연했어요.
examples.en: That conductor has performed in many countries around the world.

examples.ko: 공연이 끝나고 관객들이 지휘자에게 박수를 보냈어요.
examples.en: After the concert, the audience applauded the conductor.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 지휘자가 되는 게 꿈이었어요.
examples.en: Since I was little, my dream has been to become a conductor.

examples.ko: 소방 훈련에서는 현장 지휘자의 말을 잘 들어야 해요.
examples.en: In a fire drill, you must listen carefully to the commander on site.

explain: 주로 오케스트라나 합창단을 이끄는 사람을 말해요. 현장에서 사람들을 움직이는 '현장 지휘자'처럼 조직에서도 쓰지만, 회사의 높은 사람은 '대표'나 '팀장'이라고 해요. 악기를 연주하는 '연주자'와는 달라요.

phrases.example: 합창단 지휘자가 학생들에게 박자를 알려 줬어요.
phrases.en: The choir conductor showed the students the beat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어느 단체의 지휘자인지 앞에 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the group name before it to say whose conductor.

phrases.en: That orchestra's conductor is very famous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지휘자의 가장 대표적인 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most typical use of the word.

phrases.en: I want to become a conductor someday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 직업을 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about dreams or careers.

explain_en: It mainly means the person who leads an orchestra or choir. It can also be used for a person directing others on site, as in 현장 지휘자, but a company boss is called 대표 or 팀장. It is different from an 연주자 (performer).

examples.en: I put a lot of effort into preparing this presentation.
The cake I spent so long on turned out a failure.
I hope the results match the effort I put in.

examples.ko: 사진 한 장 찍는 데도 공들이는 친구예요.
examples.en: He's a friend who takes great care even over one photo.

examples.ko: 공들여 쓴 편지를 받으면 마음이 따뜻해져요.
examples.en: Receiving a carefully written letter warms my heart.
You don't have to put in that much effort.

explain: '공을 들이다'처럼 '을'을 넣어 말하는 경우도 많아요. '정성을 들이다'와 비슷하지만 시간과 노력을 오래 쏟았다는 느낌이 더 강해요. '공들여'는 부사처럼 뒤의 말을 꾸며 줘요.

phrases.en: I put a lot of effort into this dish.
phrases.nuance_ko: '공들이다'를 '을'을 넣어 두 단어로 쓴 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is '공들이다' written as two words with '을'.

phrases.example: 어머니가 공들여 만든 김치는 맛이 특별해요.
phrases.en: The kimchi my mother made with great care tastes special.
phrases.nuance_ko: '공들여'는 뒤의 동사를 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: '공들여' modifies the verb that follows.

phrases.en: The results will be as good as the effort you put in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 노력한 정도에 따라 결과가 나온다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the result will match the effort invested.
phrases.en_equiv: as much as you put in

explain_en: People often insert '을' and say '공을 들이다'. It is close to '정성을 들이다' but emphasizes putting in a lot of time and effort. '공들여' works like an adverb that modifies the following verb.

examples.en: I studied Korean on my own.
Self-study was hard, so I signed up for an academy.
Many people teach themselves guitar.
I'm teaching myself by watching videos.
Since you study alone, a plan is important in self-study.
He taught himself and passed the exam.

explain: '독학하다'로도 쓰고 '독학으로'를 자주 써요. 학원이나 선생님 없이 혼자 배우는 일이라서 '혼자 공부하다'보다 목표가 분명한 느낌이에요. '자습'은 학교나 학원에서 스스로 공부하는 시간을 말해요.

phrases.en: I'm teaching myself guitar.
phrases.nuance_ko: '독학'을 동사로 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 독학.

phrases.en: He passed the exam through self-study.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험이나 자격증 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for exams and certificates.

phrases.en: I study alone at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: '독학'보다 더 일상적이고 가벼운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More casual and everyday than 독학.

explain_en: It is used as '독학하다' and very often as '독학으로'. It means learning without a teacher or academy, with a clearer goal than '혼자 공부하다'. '자습' is the self-study time inside a school or academy.

t90.ax: I studied Korean on my own.
